title: Repair tenant alert delivery pipeline and normalize span monotonicity
creator: Amira Chen
description: Multiple enterprise tenants reported missing alert firings and blank alert-rule dashboards during an IPv6 rollout window. Simultaneously, trace stitching for affected tenants showed span timestamp drift causing spans to be dropped from live traces and metric-derived alert conditions to undercount. This ticket tracks the production fix, mitigation, and follow-up hardening work to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy the IPv6 routing change in telemetry ingestion cluster (staging scenario simulated).
2) Send synthetic spans and metrics with source timestamps including slight clock skews (~200ms) and intentionally reordered batches.
3) Observe that alert engine binding lookup returns empty for some tenant namespaces and alert dashboards show zero time series where data is present in raw storage.
4) Query traces: spans that have timestamp drift beyond ingest-window are not stitched and do not appear in the trace viewer.
5) Replaying the same payloads after a restart of the ingestion forwarder reproduces the missing alert bindings intermittently.
mitigation: Hotfix rolled: updated ingestion-forwarder to tolerate out-of-order batches and keep per-tenant watermark state (PR #4120).
Emergency rolling restart of the ingestion-forwarder fleet for affected region to flush inconsistent in-memory binding caches (completed at 2026-02-28 03:20 UTC).
Temporarily widened alert-engine ingestion window (+500ms) to include borderline spans while root cause analysis proceeded.
Notified affected customers and provided list of missing alert windows; created customer-specific backfill jobs for critical alerts.
root_cause: A race introduced during a telemetry routing change left some tenant alert index binds in a transient state when the forwarder processed reordered batches. Additionally, span timestamp normalization logic assumed monotonic timestamps per connection; when small clock skews were introduced by new IPv6 routing, spans arrived with non-monotonic timestamps and were dropped by the stitcher. The combination caused alerts that rely on merged time series and trace-derived metrics to miss data points.
scope: Hosted telemetry ingestion for region: eu-west-1 and a subset of Dedicated tenants using the new forwarder build. Approximately 12 tenants reported missed alerts; potential for broader unseen undercounting across multi-tenant hosts during the rollout window.

decisions: 1) Short-term: widen alert ingestion window and perform rolling restarts across affected clusters to restore eligibility for borderline spans.
2) Medium-term: add per-tenant persistent watermark store to ingestion-forwarder to survive restarts and reorderings.
3) Long-term: add monotonicity-tolerant stitcher that normalizes span timestamps using source_time and arrival_time heuristics and emits a normalization confidence score for dashboards/alerts.
next_steps: Implement persistent watermark store (ENG-230011) and add automated upgrade migration path.
Ship telemetry normalization library to handle clock skew and out-of-order spans (PR #987 in telemetry repo).
Add alerting rule to detect sudden increase in 'alert_binding_lookup_failures' and trigger automated canary rollbacks before full rollout.
Run tenant-specific backfills for the incident window and validate alert replays with customers.
